- The message was marked as Spoof with the action Reject as a result of the policy AntiPhishPolicy/REDACTED-ID being applied to the message. Antispam engineering will not accept ML false positive escalations where authentication is not passing. Even if there are some messages that fail authentication and get delivered while others do not, that doesn't change this requirement. Authentication failing isn't a guarantee we will junk a message, but fixing it is a requirement for any false positives. In the case of ML false positives, mitigation in the service requires that SPF=pass and DMARC=pass/bestguesspass. This tenant has at least one transport rule where the _ApplyHtmlDisclaimerFallbackAction_ is set to _Wrap_. When a message with an attachment is received from outside the organization, and it is processed by one of these ETRs, it is possible that Safe Attachments could find the message malicious, but still deliver it to the inbox. This 'Wrap' fallback action of the ETR interferes with ATP operation because it modifies the original message and creates a new message. When this wrapping occurs, it can cause an ATP malicious verdict to be bypassed and the message to be delivered to the inbox. Long term, the ATP team is working with the ETR team to make modifications to this functionality so that the wrap doesn't break ATP Safe Attachments functionality. Messages affected by this will typically show up as a message with the affected disclaimer and another message attached, and the attached message contains the malicious attachment. 

**Action Needed:** 

For now, we recommend that the customer modify all ETRs that append an HTML disclaimer on messages received from outside the organization to use the _ApplyHtmlDisclaimerFallbackAction_ of _Reject_, rather than _Wrap_. The customer can find any affected ETRs by running _Get-TransportRule | ?{$_.ApplyHTMLDisclaimerFallbackAction -eq 'Wrap' -and $_.FromScope -eq 'NotInOrganization'}_. 

Verdicts consist of 3 parts; the filter verdict which is the verdict our filtering software gave to the message, the tenant verdict which are any overrides the tenant applied to the message via any policy or user settings, and the final verdict which determines what happens to the message.

- Tenant Overrides: None. 
- Final Verdict: NotSpam due to filter verdict.

**ISSUE**: Mail sent to specific shared mailboxes should be allowed to forward. You are instead receiving NDR's indicating forwarding is not allowed.

**CAUSE**:

- We verified that your policy consists of the following conditions:  
  
**If the message**: Is received from 'user@REDACTED.local' or 'user@REDACTED.local' or 'user@REDACTED.local' or 'user@REDACTED.local' or 'user@REDACTED.local' or 'user@REDACTED.local' or 'user@REDACTED.local'  
 

**AND**  
 

**Is received from a member of group** 'user@REDACTED.local' or 'user@REDACTED.local' Take the following actions: Apply hosted outbound spam filter policy "External Email Forwarding".

- As your test message is sent to **user@REDACTED.local**, it meets the predicate of the '**user**' the mail is sent to. However, that user needs to be a member of one the **groups** in the 2nd predicate, which it is not.

- The policy requires both as opposed to 'either/or'. 

- Therefore, to address this, you can create a separate policy so one looks for just the users, while the other looks for just the groups.

- You have configured this while we were on the call, and it has yielded positive results

[Outbound Spam policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/outbound-spam-policies-configure?view=o365-worldwide#:~:text=Multiple%20different%20types,applied%20to%20him.)

### **Complex Routing Scenario with MX pointing to EOP**[]([internal-ticket])

The customer points MX to EOP and implemented a complex routing scenario via [Centralized Mail Transport](https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/transport-routing#route-incoming-internet-messages-through-the-exchange-online-organization)  or [Conditional Mail Routing](https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/mail-flow-best-practices/use-connectors-to-configure-mail-flow/conditional-mail-routing)  and users targeted by the Phish Simulation are hosted in EXO, emails flowing as follows:

**Issue**: You are experiencing email rejections with DMARC error for both external and internal domains, as well as printers.

**Root Cause**: This issue is caused by two recent changes in Microsoft’s email security policies:

- In July of 2023, Microsoft implemented ‘Honor DMARC’, which means that messages that fail DMARC validation and have a reject policy will be bounced back to the sender with an error message. For example, if you send an email from contoso.com and it fails DMARC validation, you will receive a non-delivery report (NDR) with the following message: 550 5.7.509: Access denied, sending domain contoso.com does not pass DMARC verification and has a DMARC policy of reject.
- In addition, Microsoft also implemented ‘Secure by Default’, which aims to block malicious URLs and high confidence phishing emails regardless of any tenant override. The only exception to this is for tenants that use third-party filtering services and do not have their MX records pointing to Office 365.

These changes affect the way your emails are processed by our service, which is not the first hop in your email routing.
